title: Legislative districts of Benguet
wikitext:
{{Short description|Legislative district of the Philippines}} {{Politics of the Philippines}} The '''legislative districts of Benguet''' are the representations of the [[Provinces of the Philippines|province]] of [[Benguet]] in the [[List of legislatures of the Philippines|various national legislatures]] of the [[Philippines]]. The province is currently represented in the [[House of Representatives of the Philippines|lower house]] of the [[Congress of the Philippines]] through its [[#Lone District|lone congressional district]]. == History == {{further|Legislative district of Mountain Province}} In 1917, the undivided [[Mountain Province]], of which Benguet was a component sub-province, was provided representation in the [[Philippine Legislature]]. Pursuant to the Revised Administrative Code (Act No. 2711) enacted on March 10, 1917, the non-Christian-majority areas of the Philippines, which then included the Mountain Province and Baguio, were to be collectively represented in the legislature's [[Philippine Senate|upper house]] by two senators from the [[Senatorial districts of the Philippines#Twelfth District|12th senatorial district]], both appointed by the [[Governor-General of the Philippines|Governor-General]]. Three assembly members, also appointed by the Governor-General, were to represent the [[Mountain Province]] and the [[Cities of the Philippines#Independent cities|chartered city]] of [[Baguio]] in the [[Philippine Assembly|lower house]] as a [[Legislative district of Mountain Province#1917–1935|single at-large district]].{{cite book|author=Philippine Legislature|title=Revised Administrative Code of the Philippine Islands of 1917 (Act No. 2711)|date=1917|publisher=Bureau of Printing|url=https://archive.org/stream/RevisedAdministrativeCodeOfThePhilippineIslandsOf1917/Revised%20Administrative%20Code%20of%20the%20Philippine%20Islands%20of%201917#page/n43/mode/2up|access-date=February 4, 2017|format=Digitized Revised Administrative Code of the Philippine Islands of 1917 from the Presidential Museum and Library Collection, uploaded on February 15, 2016}} The residents of Benguet and the rest of the Mountain Province only began electing representatives through popular vote in [[1935 Philippine general election|1935]] by virtue of Act No. 4203; the law provided the territorial coverage for each lower house representative district, while also abolishing the senatorial district system. The sub-province was then represented as part of the Mountain Province's [[Legislative districts of Mountain Province#2nd District (defunct)|second district]], which also included the city of [[Baguio]].{{cite journal|author=Philippine Legislature|title=Public Laws Enacted by the Philippine Legislature, Acts No. 4203 to 4275|journal=Public Resolutions, Etc|series=Laws, etc|date=1937|publisher=Bureau of Printing Office |page=5|url=https://babel.hathitrust.org/cgi/pt?id=mdp.35112102880830;view=1up;seq=133}} In the disruption caused by the [[Second World War]], the Mountain Province sent [[#At-Large (defunct)|two delegates]] to the [[National Assembly of the Second Philippine Republic|National Assembly]] of the Japanese-sponsored [[Second Philippine Republic]]: one was the provincial governor (an [[ex officio member|''ex officio'' member]]), while the other was elected through a provincial assembly of [[KALIBAPI]] members during the [[Japanese occupation of the Philippines]]. [[Baguio]], being a chartered city, was [[Legislative district of Baguio#At-Large (defunct)|represented separately]] in this short-lived legislative body. Upon the restoration of the [[Philippine Commonwealth]] in 1945, district representation was restored to the pre-war setup: the sub-province of [[Benguet]] and [[Baguio]] remained part of Mountain Province's [[Legislative district of Mountain Province#2nd District (defunct)|second district]]. The enactment of Republic Act No. 4695 on June 18, 1966 made the sub-province of [[Benguet]] into a full-fledged province. Per Section 10 of R.A. 4695 [[Baguio]] was to be part of the newly independent province's representative district.{{cite web|url=http://www.chanrobles.com/republicacts/republicactno4695.html|date=June 18, 1966|access-date=February 4, 2017|website=Chan Robles Law Library|author=Congress of the Philippines|title=Republic Act No. 4695 - An Act Creating the Provinces of Benguet, Mountain Province, Ifugao and Kalinga-Apayao}} Benguet, along with Baguio, began electing its separate representative starting in [[1969 Philippine general election|the next general election]]. Benguet was represented in the [[Interim Batasang Pambansa]] as part of [[Interim Batasang Pambansa#Regional Representatives|Region I]] from 1978 to 1984. The province returned [[#At-Large (defunct)|one representative, elected at-large]], to the [[Regular Batasang Pambansa]] in [[1984 Philippine parliamentary election|1984]]. [[Baguio]] separately elected its [[Legislative district of Baguio#At-Large (defunct)|own representative]] in this election. Under the new Constitution{{cite web|title=1987 Constitution of the Philippines - Apportionment Ordinance|url=https://www.officialgazette.gov.ph/constitutions/the-1987-constitution-of-the-republic-of-the-philippines/the-1987-constitution-of-the-republic-of-the-philippines-ordinance/|author=1986 Constitutional Commission|date=February 2, 1987|access-date=June 13, 2016}} which was proclaimed on February 11, 1987, Benguet was once more grouped with Baguio. The latter, though an independent city since 1909, comprised what was legally known between 1987 and 1995 as the [[#1st District (defunct)|first district of Benguet]], while the actual province itself comprised the [[#2nd District (defunct)|second district]]. Both elected members to the restored House of Representatives starting [[1987 Philippine legislative election|that same year]]. Starting in [[1995 Philippine general election|1995]] the [[#1st District (defunct)|first district]] was re-designated as the "[[Legislative district of Baguio]]", thereby making the [[#2nd District (defunct)|second district]] Benguet's [[#Lone District|lone district]]. Since 2019, the districts used in appropriation of members is coextensive with the legislative districts of Benguet.
